ground_truth.description: BaseAuth.recoverSapientSignature returns bytes32(uint256(1)) instead of actual signer imageHash, violating ISapient interface. Breaks Merkle leaf construction in BaseSig.recoverBranch.
ground_truth.root_cause: BaseAuth.recoverSapientSignature returns bytes32(uint256(1)) instead of actual signer imageHash, violating ISapient interface. Breaks Merkle leaf construction in BaseSig.recoverBranch.
ground_truth.attack_scenario: Wallet uses another wallet as sapient signer → signature validation fails due to incorrect image hash. PoC: Add test to test/modules/BaseSig.t.sol: test_BaseAuth_recoverSapientSignature_ReturnsConstant. Deploys MinimalSapient, crafts signature, asserts constant return.
ground_truth.fix_description: Return actual image hash from recoverSapientSignature. Extend signatureValidation to return imageHash or call BaseSig.recover.

vulnerabilities.explanation: The function violates the ISapient interface by returning a constant value `bytes32(uint256(1))` instead of the actual image hash that was validated. This breaks downstream functionality that expects the actual image hash for Merkle tree operations.
vulnerabilities.attack_scenario: When a wallet uses another wallet as a sapient signer, calling recoverSapientSignature will return a fixed value (0x0...01) instead of the actual image hash. Any downstream system expecting the real image hash for Merkle branch construction in BaseSig.recoverBranch will fail or operate incorrectly, breaking the intended multi-wallet authentication flow.
vulnerabilities.suggested_fix: Return the actual image hash that was validated during signature processing. The function should extract and return the correct imageHash rather than returning a hardcoded value.

prediction.overall_explanation: The contract contains a critical logic error in the recoverSapientSignature function that returns a constant value instead of the actual validated image hash. This breaks the intended sapient signer functionality and violates the ISapient interface contract, potentially causing failures in Merkle-based authentication flows.
